findings.title: Permission denials are cached for 30s with no invalidation, so a newly granted permission stays denied
findings.body: When the DB check returns not-allowed, the result is stored in permDenialCache for shortCacheTTL (30s), keyed by user, action, name and parent folder. Nothing invalidates this entry when permissions change. The PR's stated goal is that a creator can access a dashboard or folder they just created. If the user is first denied on that name (for example a fetch before creation), the denial is then served from cache for up to 30s even though the DB now grants access. The denial cache check at line 116-121 returns before the DB fallback runs, so the new-permission fallback never applies during that window. Either skip caching denials, use a much shorter TTL, or invalidate the entry when a permission or resource is created.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because fields are joined with '_' and names can contain '_'
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates name and parent with '_' separators without escaping. Different tuples produce the same key, e.g. name="a_", parent="b" and name="a", parent="_b" both yield "...action_a__b". A denial recorded for one resource then short-circuits Check for another resource with a colliding key, returning a wrong deny. Dashboard and folder UIDs can contain underscores, so this can happen. Use an unambiguous encoding (length prefix, or a separator that cannot appear in UIDs).

findings.title: Folder tree stays cached for 30s after folder creation, so inherited access to new nested folders is denied
findings.body: buildFolderTree caches the namespace folder tree for shortCacheTTL and nothing invalidates it on folder creation. The fallback to the DB only refreshes permissions, not the folder tree. For a folder created within the TTL, e.g. grandchild C under a newly created child B under a folder A the user already has access to, the tree lacks C (and possibly B). checkInheritedPermissions then calls tree.Ancestors(C), which cannot reach A, so the creator is denied on a dashboard in C even though they hold a grant on A. This is the same user-facing bug the PR aims to fix, and it is not covered by the new fallback. Refresh the folder tree on a miss for the requested folder, or invalidate it on folder creation.

findings.title: New cache tests do not cover the behaviour the PR is meant to fix
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck covers cache hits, DB fallback on a miss or outdated map, and a pre-set explicit denial. It never checks that a DB denial populates the denial cache, nor that a permission granted after a denial is honoured (the creator scenario). It also has no test for inherited access through a folder created after the tree was cached, and no test for denial key collisions. These are the scenarios that would catch the staleness and key issues above.
